verdict: Magento: Choose Magento when catalog/B2B complexity and control outweigh SaaS simplicity — and you have budget for hosting and a competent integrator. Scores use the Ecommerce editorial methodology from first-party research as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing.
strengths: Deep catalog and B2B capability for complex merchants
Open Source license avoids a SaaS subscription on the core
Enterprise path via Adobe Commerce when GMV and B2B justify it
Composable / headless options for ambitious stacks
weaknesses: High hosting, security, and agency TCO
Steep learning curve vs hosted SaaS
bestFor: Mid-market and enterprise catalogs with complex B2B needs
Merchants who outgrew WooCommerce simplicity and need deeper commerce core
notIdealFor: Solo founders wanting a weekend store launch
Website-first brands that mainly need pages + light commerce (see Wix/Squarespace)
Buyers who need published monthly plan tiles only
tradeoffs: Subscription floors vs payment-processing spreads and GMV/overage fees
App/extension TCO vs native feature depth
Open-source/hosting flexibility vs SaaS operational simplicity
Dropshipping product caps vs catalog automation depth
recommendation: Choose Magento when catalog/B2B complexity and control outweigh SaaS simplicity — and you have budget for hosting and a competent integrator. Consider WooCommerce for WordPress-native open-source SMB stacks; Shopify/BigCommerce for hosted SaaS; Wix/Squarespace for website-first light commerce.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Powerful but developer/agency-heavy — Magento is not a guided SMB launch admin like Shopify or Wix.
Core job is commerce storefront operations with deep catalog and B2B surfaces — primary open-source enterprise path.
Catalog, multi-store, and B2B depth are Magento strengths versus website builders.
Checkout is capable and extensible; conversion quality depends on theme/agency work, not a Shop Pay default.
Large extension marketplace and API surface; quality varies by integrator.
POS is possible via extensions/partners — not a Square-class bundle.
Designed for complex, high-GMV catalogs and multi-brand enterprise programmes.
Open Source license is free but TCO (hosting + agency) is high; Adobe Commerce quotes compress value for SMBs.
Adobe Sensei / recommendations appear on Commerce paths — not the Open Source default.

overallScoreRationale: Weighted average of the nine ecommerce editorial criteria using category weights (storefront/commerce fit 15, catalog/orders 14, ease 12, checkout 12, integrations 12, value 12, omnichannel/POS 10, scalability 9, AI 6), rounded to 1 decimal. Products are scored inside their job cluster — SaaS platforms, open-source carts, omnichannel POS bundles, and dropshipping sourcing apps are not forced into one undifferentiated ranking. Not a hands-on lab score; affiliate economics are excluded.
